body:
herdr.dev, read in round 2. Human-facing shape: a space per repo, a tab per task; the sidebar and tab show which agent is working, done or waiting; agents run in herdr-core so quitting the app changes nothing; machines over SSH appear in the same sidebar; layout, keys and theme are plain files an agent can edit; status via OSC 7501; open source (herdr-core, herdr-app, herdr TUI).

It is the same product hypothesis as zmux with a custom server, a custom protocol and a custom config language underneath. The 'infinitely lazier' version keeps the nouns (spaces, tabs, who-needs-me, survives-close) and takes the substrate from zmx: no core, labels instead of a store, `zmx set` instead of OSC, existing files instead of a config tree.
title: herdr: the inspiring nouns, and the server we probably refuse
